messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-queue-growth-high for pool=redwood-gen2 region=us-west-2. queue_length=1243, p99_latency=2340ms, 429_rate=18% :rotating_light:
jamie: i'm on it — pulling metrics now. any obvious recent changes?
maria: I'm seeing sustained queue growth starting ~2167777000. 429s start rising at the same time. model affected=redwood-v1-large (hosted). autoscaler errors show 'scale_limit_reached' for pool redwood-gen2.
eli: logs from autoscaler: 
```
ERROR autoscaler.go:210 scale_up failed: hit_pool_max (poolCapacity=24, desired=28)
WARN autoscaler.go:332 backoff until 2167777800
```
jamie: so autoscaler wanted more nodes but pool cap blocked it. why is desired jump so large? check batching/caching.
ken: I pushed a batching config tweak earlier this morning — experimental bump to max_batch_delay_ms from 12 -> 120 to try to increase throughput for small requests. I reverted locally but maybe not in all clusters. commit c3f2b9.
maria: also noticed prefix_cache_ttl was changed in the same commit from 300 -> 30 to reduce memory. that will increase prefix cache misses and kill KV cache hit rates. hitrate dropped from 82% -> 12% around the same time.
jamie: that combo makes sense: bigger max delay = larger, longer batches but because prefix cache misses drop, runtime spends more time recomputing KV cache and throughput collapses -> backlog. autoscaler sees queued requests and requests more nodes but pool cap prevents scale.
eli: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) rollback batching change, 2) increase pool capacity temporarily, 3) bump prefix_cache_ttl back and flush caches, 4) route heavy customers to fallback model.
maria: i'm on rollback of batching config to previous commit now (reverting c3f2b9). doing a staged config rollout to us-west-2 first.
deploy-bot: deploy started: config-rollout/rollback-batching c3f2b9 -> reverted. scope=us-west-2.
jamie: infra action: can we temporarily raise pool cap so autoscaler can actually spin up nodes while we stabilize?
eli: running infractl now:
```
infractl pool update --name redwood-gen2 --max-capacity 40 --region us-west-2
```
infra-bot: infractl accepted job id=job-98432, expected time ~90s.
ken: i'll also push a prefix_cache_ttl revert (30 -> 300) and flush the cache after. preparing patch.
maria: applied revert to prefix_cache_ttl. rolling to us-west-2.
deploy-bot: config apply complete: prefix_cache_ttl=300 rolled to 6/6 nodes in us-west-2.
ken: flushing prefix caches on inference pods: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference exec -l app=inference -c runtime -- sh -c "curl -XPOST http://localhost:9000/cache/flush"
```
jamie: started routing rule: divert top-5 tenants with highest qps on redwood-v1-large -> redwood-v1-medium until metrics settle.
cs-rep: ping — which customers impacted? need a short note for support.
jamie: initial impact: ~18% 429 rate overall for redwood-v1-large in us-west-2, about 32 tenants with >95th percentile request failures during window. streaming latency p99 rose to ~2.3s. will compile list and hand to you in 10m.
eli: autoscaler made progress after cap bump, new nodes joining: +8 nodes accepted, pool now at 32/40. queue length trending down: 1243 -> 410 in 6 minutes.
maria: after prefix cache revert and flush, KV hitrate climbing back to ~76% and runtime CPU drop observed. good sign.
jamie: latency p95 now 680ms, p99 1.1s — still elevated but improving. 429 rate down to 4%.
ken: confirm: batching rollback fully rolled out to us-west-2. we'll hold the original experiment behind a feature flag and run smaller A/B.
deploy-bot: rollout: config-rollout/rollback-batching completed.
cs-rep: thanks — I'll start triage messages to the 32 affected tenants and offer temporary routing to medium model.
jamie: oncall handoff plan: i'll monitor for 20m, then hand to alex for overnight if stable. alex are you available?
alex: available — i'll take the next watch. please add summary and links to dashboards.
jamie: quick summary for incident note: cause = recent config regression (batching max_batch_delay_ms increased + prefix_cache_ttl lowered) -> prefix cache miss storm -> throughput collapse -> queue growth -> autoscaler desired nodes exceeded pool cap causing scale failure and throttling. mitigations applied: batching rollback, prefix_cache_ttl revert + flush, temporary pool cap increase, manual scale-up + routing heavy tenants to fallback model. status = recovering, queue decreasing, KV hitrate recovering, customers notified. follow-ups: postmortem + revert-safe gating for batching experiments, autoscaler alert to include pool-cap hit metric, and automated canary for prefix_cache hitrate.
eli: agree. i'll open the incident postmortem doc and add timeline + logs.
jamie: handing to alex at 2167778200. thanks team. :thumbsup:
alex: taking over. tagging cs-rep for followups. keep pager open if we see regressions.
